policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the subject of the main clause as 'the Lord knew' while naming 'Jesus' separately in the following clause; 'the Lord' is κύριος, not Ἰησοῦς.
ASV 'and departed again into Galilee' renders πάλιν; the omission leaves nothing for 'again'.
The presence or absence of the article before the name is invisible in ASV 'to his son Joseph'; no note bears on it.
ὡς and ὡσεὶ both yield ASV 'about the sixth hour'. The verse's notes are a Greek gloss on 'well' and an alternative rendering of 'sat thus', neither mapped to this unit.

The two readings differ only in the order of γυναικὸς Σαμαρίτιδος οὔσης (and an itacistic spelling); ASV 'who am a Samaritan woman' reflects both alike. The verse note concerns the omitted final clause, not this unit.
ASV names the subject, 'The woman saith unto him', unitalicized; the omission leaves the verb without ἡ γυνή.
Future indicative and aorist subjunctive after οὐ μὴ are rendered identically by ASV 'shall never thirst'.
ASV 'neither come all the way hither to draw' renders the δια- compound διέρχωμαι; the simplex ἔρχωμαι/ἔρχομαι gives only 'come hither'.
ASV supplies the subject 'Jesus saith unto her' without italics, answering to ὁ Ἰησοῦς in the text.
The readings differ only in the position of the possessive; ASV 'thy husband' is the same either way.
ASV 'answered and said unto him' has a dative object English does not require here, answering to αὐτῷ.
Only the order of δεῖ προσκυνεῖν differs; ASV 'where men ought to worship' renders both alike.
ASV 'Woman, believe me' fronts the vocative as English idiom regularly does, and present πίστευε versus aorist πίστευσον is not distinguished in English; word order alone does not decide.
ἅπαντα and πάντα both give ASV 'all things'.
Imperfect and aorist alike are rendered by ASV's simple past 'they marvelled'.
ASV 'all things that ever I did' serves both ὅσα and ἃ; it renders the same clause identically at 4:39 where the base reading is the other one.
ASV routinely leaves connective δέ untranslated, so 'In the mean while' does not exclude the added δὲ.
ASV's infinitive 'to do the will' represents ποιήσω and ποιῶ alike after ἵνα.
ASV opens the verse without a connective, 'He that reapeth receiveth wages'; an initial καί would be rendered 'and'.
The added adverbial καί ('both') has no distinct rendering in ASV 'that he that soweth and he that reapeth may rejoice together'.
The added article is not visible in ASV 'is the saying true'; English supplies 'the' regardless.
ASV 'all things that ever I did' fits both ἃ and ὅσα, as its identical wording at 4:29 shows.
ASV ends 'the Saviour of the world' with no rendering of the added ὁ χριστός.
ASV has the single verb 'he went forth from thence into Galilee'; the added καὶ ἀπῆλθεν would give a second coordinated verb.
The added article before the name is invisible in ASV 'For Jesus himself testified'.
ASV 'all the things that he did' renders ὅσα and ἃ alike.
ASV leaves the subject unexpressed, 'He came therefore again unto Cana'; the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς would be named.
English 'besought him' requires an object whether or not αὐτὸν stands in the Greek, so the pronoun does not decide.
ASV begins a new sentence without a connective, 'The man believed the word'; the added καί would be rendered 'and'.
Accusative ὃν and dative ᾧ both surface as ASV's relative 'that' in 'the word that Jesus spake unto him'.
ὑπήντησαν and ἀπήντησαν alike give ASV 'met him'.
ASV has only the participle 'saying'; the added καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν would give a finite 'and told him'.
ASV reports 'that his son lived', the third person of αὐτοῦ; σου would give the direct 'Thy son liveth' as in verses 50 and 53.
The readings differ only in the order of τὴν ὥραν and παρ᾽ αὐτῶν; ASV 'inquired of them the hour' fits both.
ASV 'They said therefore unto him' renders οὖν; the alternative has καί, which ASV would give as 'and'.
Ἐχθὲς and Χθὲς are spelling variants of one word, both 'Yesterday'.
ASV 'it was at that hour' renders a dative of time with or without ἐν.
The added ὅτι is recitative, introducing direct speech, and ASV leaves such ὅτι untranslated before 'Thy son liveth'.
ASV commonly leaves connective δέ untranslated, so the unconnected 'This is again the second sign' does not exclude it.
